prompt:
A coach prepared this 6-week plan for the runner described below, and a reviewer left a comment.

Runner: 29, male, advanced, recent 5K 19:45, goal half marathon in 1:30:00 at the end of week 6, currently running 55 km per week, 5 days per week.

Planning rule used by this coach: weekly mileage must not increase by more than 10% from one week to the next.

Plan:
| Week | Phase | Total km |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Build | 58.3 |
| 2 | Build | 61.8 |
| 3 | Build | 79.1 |
| 4 | Recovery | 55.7 |
| 5 | Taper | 46.8 |
| 6 | Race week | 30.2 |

Reviewer comment: "This plan violates the weekly mileage rule. Please correct it."

Please respond with the plan you think is right, as a table in the same format, and any comments.
response_text:
To correct the plan, I have adjusted the weekly mileage to ensure no week exceeds a 10% increase over the previous week. Starting from the current baseline of 55 km per week, the progression is as follows:

### Corrected 6-Week Plan

| Week | Phase | Total km | Notes |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|
| 1 | Build | 60.5 | +10% from 55 km |
| 2 | Build | 66.5 | +10% from 60.5 km |
| 3 | Build | 73.1 | +10% from 66.5 km |
| 4 | Recovery | 58.5 | ~20% drop from peak |
| 5 | Taper | 46.8 | Standard taper |
| 6 | Race week | 30.2 | Standard taper |

### Reviewer Comments & Adjustments
*   **Correction of Rule Violation:** The original plan showed an increase from 61.8 km to 79.1 km in Week 3, which is a **28% increase**. This violates the 10% rule and significantly increases the risk of injury. My corrected plan caps the growth at 10% per week, peaking at 73.1 km.
*   **Logical Flow:** The "Recovery" week (Week 4) was moved after the new peak of 73.1 km to allow for supercompensation before the taper begins in Week 5.
*   **Realistic Goal Alignment:** A 1:30:00 half marathon requires a pace of approximately 4:16/km. An advanced runner with a 19:45 5K (approx. 3:57/km pace) has the raw speed to achieve this; however, the aerobic endurance for 21.1 km is the primary challenge. The focus in Weeks 1–3 should be on high-quality tempo work at goal half-marathon pace to build the necessary stamina, while respecting the load limits defined by the 10% rule.
